findings.title: CORS allows all origins with credentials
findings.userExplanation: Your server accepts requests from any website AND allows those sites to send user cookies. A malicious page can act as your logged-in users. Restrict CORS to your own domain.
findings.technicalExplanation: cors() is configured with a wildcard/true origin and credentials: true, enabling cross-site authenticated requests (CSRF-equivalent). Set an explicit origin allowlist.
findings.fixHint: Pass an explicit allowlist to cors(), e.g. cors({ origin: ['https://yourapp.com'], credentials: true }). Never combine a wildcard origin with credentials.

findings.title: API route writes to the database without an authentication check
findings.userExplanation: This API endpoint changes data in your database, but the code never checks who is making the request. Anyone who calls the endpoint can modify your data. Verify the user's session before performing the write.
findings.technicalExplanation: server.js performs 1 database mutation(s) in a handler that contains no effective auth guard (a session lookup or token verification whose result is checked) — and neither its module scope nor its resolved imports do. Add a session check before the mutation and return 401 when absent.
findings.fixHint: At the top of the handler, resolve the caller's identity (getServerSession(), supabase.auth.getUser(), or jwt.verify on the request token), return a 401 response when it is missing, and only then run the mutation.

findings.title: Delete operation without ownership check
findings.evidence: await db.query('DELETE FROM items WHERE id = $1', [req.params.id]);
findings.userExplanation: A SQL DELETE removes rows without a trusted ownership check. Add the signed-in user to the WHERE clause using a server-side identity so users can only delete their own records.
findings.technicalExplanation: Raw SQL DELETE at server.js:16 filters on "id = $1" with no ownership column bound to a trusted identity. Append e.g. AND user_id = $trustedUserId.
findings.fixHint: Verify the session first, then scope the delete by the trusted user id (e.g. .eq("user_id", session.user.id), where: { id, userId: session.user.id }, or AND user_id = $trustedUserId) so users can only delete rows they own.

findings.title: No security headers configured
findings.evidence: No security header configuration found in this Express project
findings.userExplanation: Your app does not appear to set security headers like Content-Security-Policy or X-Frame-Options. These headers protect users from clickjacking and script-injection attacks and are quick to add.
findings.technicalExplanation: The Express app does not use helmet or set security headers manually. Add app.use(helmet()) as a baseline.
findings.fixHint: Install helmet (npm i helmet) and add app.use(helmet()) before your routes for sensible defaults. If you enable helmet's Content-Security-Policy, tailor the directives to the assets your app loads and test in report-only mode first, since a default/blanket CSP can break inline scripts, styles, and third-party embeds.
